name: Fire Engine Red
lede: Fire Engine Red is a bright, vivid red, a descriptive name that points to the red of fire engines.

sections.title: A vivid red
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary defines fire engine red as a bright vivid red, and lists it with a family of fire-named reds: fire-orange, a reddish orange, and fire-red, a color on Ignaz Schiffermüller's colour wheel, where it appears as *feueroth* beside fire-blue [1][2]. The same dictionary also lists FireBrick, a light maroon among the 140 X11 colors with the hex code #B22222 [1].

St Clair notes a different use: children who mix fire-engine red, sky blue and other favorite paints expecting something special instead get a murky dark grey [3]. The cause is that each added pigment subtracts more light.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: #CE2029 is close to [[bright-red]] and [[scarlet]] in the screen data [9]. The books give no date for the name [1][2]. The concordance of 29 color books finds only four strong mentions of this name, so the article stays short rather than pad the record [9]. Screen colors are approximate, and the swatch is a reference value, not a measured pigment [9].
